title: Every morning my neighbor waves at me from his window. He moved out last spring.
story:
My apartment faces a small courtyard, and across it is Mr. Alvarez's window, third floor. Every morning at 7:15 he waves at me while I make coffee. A slow, friendly wave.

I always waved back. It was nice. It made me feel like somebody noticed me.

Last week the landlord mentioned, in passing, that unit 3C had been empty since March. Mr. Alvarez had moved to Arizona. The apartment was being repainted.

I laughed it off. I said maybe a painter was waving.

The next morning at 7:15, I looked. The window was bare. No curtains, a ladder inside. And in the glass stood a figure, tall and dark, waving.

I didn't wave back.

The figure stopped. It tilted its head. Then it raised one hand, with two fingers up.

The next day, three fingers. Then four. Then five.

I started counting the days since I stopped waving. I realized the fingers weren't a greeting, they were a count, and that I'd missed the first number.

This morning at 7:15, the figure held up no fingers at all.

It pointed across the courtyard, then down, at the floor of my apartment.

The floor creaked, right behind me.
premise: waving neighbor in empty apartment across courtyard; the wave counts down
